claim: The clathrin adaptor complex AP2 is thought to be an obligate heterotetramer.
source: The clathrin adaptor complex AP2 is thought to be an obligate heterotetramer.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus about AP2 structure.

claim: α-adaptin mutants in C. elegans are viable.
source: We identify null mutations in the α subunit of AP2 in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans. α-adaptin mutants are viable and the remaining μ2/β hemicomplex retains some function.
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental observations of viable α-adaptin mutants.

claim: In α-adaptin mutants, the remaining μ2/β hemicomplex retains some function.
source: α-adaptin mutants are viable and the remaining μ2/β hemicomplex retains some function.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on experimental observations of mutant phenotypes.

claim: In μ2 mutants, the alpha/sigma2 hemicomplex is localized and is partially functional.
source: Conversely, in μ2 mutants, the alpha/sigma2 hemicomplex is localized and is partially functional.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on experimental observations of mutant phenotypes and localization studies.

claim: α-μ2 double mutants disrupt both halves of the AP2 complex and are lethal.
source: α-μ2 double mutants disrupt both halves of the complex and are lethal.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on experimental observations of double mutant viability.

claim: The lethality of α-μ2 double mutants can be rescued by expression of AP2 components in the skin.
source: The lethality can be rescued by expression of AP2 components in the skin, which allowed us to evaluate the requirement for AP2 subunits at synapses.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on experimental rescue experiments.

claim: Mutations in either α or μ2 subunits alone reduce the number of synaptic vesicles by about 30%.
source: Mutations in either α or μ2 subunits alone reduce the number of synaptic vesicles by about 30%; however, simultaneous loss of both α and μ2 subunits leads to a 70% reduction in synaptic vesicles and the presence of large vacuoles.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on electron microscopy quantification data.

claim: Simultaneous loss of both α and μ2 subunits leads to a 70% reduction in synaptic vesicles.
source: Mutations in either α or μ2 subunits alone reduce the number of synaptic vesicles by about 30%; however, simultaneous loss of both α and μ2 subunits leads to a 70% reduction in synaptic vesicles and the presence of large vacuoles.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on electron microscopy quantification data.

claim: Simultaneous loss of both α and μ2 subunits leads to the presence of large vacuoles at synapses.
source: Mutations in either α or μ2 subunits alone reduce the number of synaptic vesicles by about 30%; however, simultaneous loss of both α and μ2 subunits leads to a 70% reduction in synaptic vesicles and the presence of large vacuoles.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on electron microscopy observations.

claim: AP2 may function as two partially independent hemicomplexes.
source: These data suggest that AP2 may function as two partially independent hemicomplexes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Many cargo proteins are recruited to sites of endocytosis by the tetrameric adaptor complex AP2.
source: Many cargo proteins are recruited to sites of endocytosis by the tetrameric adaptor complex AP2 (Mahaffey et al., 1990; Traub, 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The adaptor complex AP2 recruits the coat protein clathrin to the membrane.
source: The adaptor complex in turn recruits the coat protein clathrin to the membrane.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about AP2 function.

claim: Clathrin converts the raft of cargo and adaptor proteins into a budding vesicle by forming a scaffold that shapes the membrane.
source: Clathrin converts the raft of cargo and adaptor proteins into a budding vesicle by forming a scaffold that shapes the membrane (Mashl and Bruinsma, 1998).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The predominant mechanism for synaptic vesicle endocytosis is thought to be mediated via AP2 and clathrin.
source: Nonetheless, the predominant mechanism for synaptic vesicle endocytosis is thought to be mediated via AP2 and clathrin (Dittman and Ryan, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The AP2 adaptin complex has four subunits—two large subunits α and β2, a medium subunit μ2, and a small subunit σ2.
source: The AP2 adaptin complex has four subunits—two large subunits α and β2, a medium subunit μ2, and a small subunit σ2 (Matsui and Kirchhausen, 1990).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: It is generally thought that adaptor complexes act as obligate tetramers.
source: It is generally thought that adaptor complexes act as obligate tetramers; loss of one subunit will destabilize the entire complex (Dell'Angelica et al., 1998; Kantheti et al., 1998; Collins et al., 2002; Motley et al., 2003; Traub, 2003; Nakatsu et al., 2004; Mitsunari et al., 2005; Kim and Ryan, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Loss of one AP2 subunit will destabilize the entire complex.
source: It is generally thought that adaptor complexes act as obligate tetramers; loss of one subunit will destabilize the entire complex (Dell'Angelica et al., 1998; Kantheti et al., 1998; Collins et al., 2002; Motley et al., 2003; Traub, 2003; Nakatsu et al., 2004; Mitsunari et al., 2005; Kim and Ryan, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: AP2 functions at the plasma membrane as an interaction hub for transmembrane cargoes, accessory proteins, and clathrin.
source: AP2 functions at the plasma membrane as an interaction hub for transmembrane cargoes, accessory proteins, and clathrin (Traub, 2003; Robinson, 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A null allele in α-adaptin is lethal in Drosophila embryos.
source: A null allele in α-adaptin is lethal and leads to an absence of synaptic vesicles at neuromuscular junctions in Drosophila embryos and thus appears to disrupt endocytosis (Gonzalez-Gaitan and Jackle, 1997).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: A null allele in α-adaptin leads to an absence of synaptic vesicles at neuromuscular junctions in Drosophila embryos.
source: A null allele in α-adaptin is lethal and leads to an absence of synaptic vesicles at neuromuscular junctions in Drosophila embryos and thus appears to disrupt endocytosis (Gonzalez-Gaitan and Jackle, 1997).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: In C. elegans, loss of either α- or β-adaptin by RNA interference perturbs the endocytosis of yolk protein from the plasma membrane.
source: Similarly, in C. elegans loss of either of α- or β-adaptin by RNA interference perturbs the endocytosis of yolk protein from the plasma membrane (Grant and Hirsh, 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The medium subunit μ2 may not play an essential role for the endocytosis of synaptic vesicle components from the plasma membrane.
source: Recent data suggest that the medium subunit μ2 may not play an essential role for the endocytosis of synaptic vesicle components from the plasma membrane (Gu et al., 2008; Kim and Ryan, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: μ2 is required in part for the localization of clathrin at synapses.
source: Although μ2 is required in part for the localization of clathrin at synapses (Gu et al., 2008), synaptic vesicles and constituent proteins are still recycled in the absence of μ2 (Gu et al., 2008; Kim and Ryan, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Synaptic vesicles and constituent proteins are still recycled in the absence of μ2.
source: Although μ2 is required in part for the localization of clathrin at synapses (Gu et al., 2008), synaptic vesicles and constituent proteins are still recycled in the absence of μ2 (Gu et al., 2008; Kim and Ryan, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In C. elegans, α-adaptin is encoded by the apa-2 gene.
source: In C. elegans, α-adaptin is encoded by the apa-2 gene (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement supported by Figure 1A showing the genetic map.

claim: The apa-2 allele b1044 is a 925 bp deletion that starts within the second intron, extends to the fourth exon and deletes a large fraction of the trunk domain.
source: b1044 is a 925 bp deletion that starts within the second intron, extends to the fourth exon and deletes a large fraction of the trunk domain.
evidence: This is a direct statement describing the molecular nature of the mutation.

claim: The apa-2 allele ox422 is a premature stop mutation at Lys215.
source: ox422 is premature stop mutation at Lys215 and would lead to a truncation of α-adaptin from the middle of the trunk domain to the carboxy terminus including the ear domain (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a direct statement describing the molecular nature of the mutation, supported by Figure 1C.

claim: The ox422 mutation would lead to a truncation of α-adaptin from the middle of the trunk domain to the carboxy terminus including the ear domain.
source: ox422 is premature stop mutation at Lys215 and would lead to a truncation of α-adaptin from the middle of the trunk domain to the carboxy terminus including the ear domain (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the molecular nature of the mutation.

claim: Full-length APA-2 protein was not detected from either the b1044 or ox422 alleles.
source: We did not detect full-length APA-2 protein from either of these alleles (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), and they are likely to be null mutations.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The apa-2 alleles b1044 and ox422 are likely to be null mutations.
source: We did not detect full-length APA-2 protein from either of these alleles (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), and they are likely to be null mutations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of full-length protein.

claim: The apa-2 gene appears to be expressed in most cells of the animal.
source: The apa-2 gene appears to be expressed in most cells of the animal, and is highly expressed in the nervous system (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on GFP reporter expression patterns shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: The apa-2 gene is highly expressed in the nervous system.
source: The apa-2 gene appears to be expressed in most cells of the animal, and is highly expressed in the nervous system (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on GFP reporter expression patterns shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: Unlike α-adaptin mutants in Drosophila, worms missing α-adaptin in C. elegans are viable.
source: Unlike α-adaptin mutants in Drosophila (Gonzalez-Gaitan and Jackle, 1997), worms missing α-adaptin in C. elegans are viable; they grow to adulthood and are grossly similar to μ2-adaptin (apm-2) mutants (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a direct statement comparing C. elegans to Drosophila, supported by Figure 3A.

claim: About 30% of α mutants have cuticle protrusions on either side of the head called 'jowls'.
source: About 30% of α mutants (Figure 3A) and about 5% of μ2 mutants (Gu et al., 2008) have cuticle protrusions on either side of the head called 'jowls'.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on phenotypic observations shown in Figure 3A.

claim: About 5% of μ2 mutants have cuticle protrusions on either side of the head called 'jowls'.
source: About 30% of α mutants (Figure 3A) and about 5% of μ2 mutants (Gu et al., 2008) have cuticle protrusions on either side of the head called 'jowls'.
evidence: This is a direct statement supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The variable dumpy phenotype of apa-2 is less severe than that of apm-2.
source: However, the variable dumpy phenotype of apa-2 is less severe than that of apm-2 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on body length measurements shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The α-adaptin mutants are egg-laying defective.
source: The α-adaptin mutants are egg-laying defective and mildly uncoordinated; they crawl forward well but are slightly jerky as they move backward.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on phenotypic observations.

claim: The α-adaptin mutants are mildly uncoordinated.
source: The α-adaptin mutants are egg-laying defective and mildly uncoordinated; they crawl forward well but are slightly jerky as they move backward.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on phenotypic observations.

claim: apa-2 mutants exhibit only mild defects in thrashing when placed in liquid.
source: apa-2 mutants exhibit only mild defects in thrashing when placed in liquid (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on locomotion assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Expression of APA-2::GFP under a ubiquitous promoter can fully rescue the mutant phenotypes including the cuticle protrusions.
source: Expression of APA-2::GFP under a ubiquitous promoter can fully rescue the mutant phenotypes including the cuticle protrusions (Figure 3A–C; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on rescue experiment data shown in Figures 3A-C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of α-adaptin specifically in the epidermis rescues the cuticle phenotype.
source: Expression of the α-adaptin specifically in the epidermis (the equivalent of skin in C. elegans) rescues the cuticle phenotype (Figure 3A; Figure 3—figure supplement 1), which is similar to rescue experiments in μ2-adaptin mutants (Gu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on tissue-specific rescue experiments shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The dumpy phenotype of apa-2 is rescued by neuron-specific but not skin-specific expression.
source: However unlike μ2-adaptin mutants, the dumpy phenotype of apa-2 is rescued by neuron-specific but not skin-specific expression (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on tissue-specific rescue experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The neuron-rescued apa-2 worms are longer than the wild type.
source: In fact, the neuron-rescued worms are longer than the wild type (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on body length measurements shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Only 4.3% of the apa-2 apm-2 double mutants coming from a heterozygote are viable.
source: Indeed, when the apa-2 and apm-2 mutations are combined, only 4.3% of the double mutants coming from a heterozygote are viable and the brood size of these survivors is reduced to 1.4% compared to the wild type (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on viability data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: The brood size of apa-2 apm-2 double mutant survivors is reduced to 1.4% compared to the wild type.
source: Indeed, when the apa-2 and apm-2 mutations are combined, only 4.3% of the double mutants coming from a heterozygote are viable and the brood size of these survivors is reduced to 1.4% compared to the wild type (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on brood size data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: The rare apa-2 apm-2 double mutant escapers grow twice as slowly as wild-type animals.
source: The rare escapers grow twice as slowly as wild-type animals and are sick and dumpy (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on developmental timing data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The rare apa-2 apm-2 double mutant escapers are sick and dumpy.
source: The rare escapers grow twice as slowly as wild-type animals and are sick and dumpy (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on phenotypic observations shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Residual function of AP2 remains in both apa-2 and apm-2 single mutants.
source: These data suggest residual function of AP2 remains in both apa-2 and apm-2 single mutants.
evidence: This is an inference based on the synthetic lethality of the double mutant.

claim: Yolk is a lipoprotein particle composed of lipids and lipid-transport proteins called vitellogenins.
source: Yolk is a lipoprotein particle composed of lipids and lipid-transport proteins called vitellogenins.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about yolk composition.

claim: Yolk particles are synthesized and secreted by the intestine and are then taken up from the extracellular space by maturing oocytes via receptor-mediated endocytosis.
source: Yolk particles are synthesized and secreted by the intestine and are then taken up from the extracellular space by maturing oocytes via receptor-mediated endocytosis.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about yolk trafficking.

claim: Yolk endocytosis is clathrin-dependent.
source: Yolk endocytosis is clathrin-dependent and can be assayed in animals expressing GFP-tagged vitellogenin-2 (YP170::GFP) (Grant and Hirsh, 1999; Sato et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In wild-type worms, YP170::GFP is enriched in the three most mature oocytes near the spermatheca.
source: In wild-type worms, YP170::GFP is enriched in the three most mature oocytes near the spermatheca.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on experimental observations.

claim: In α-adaptin mutants, the number of GFP-positive oocytes is decreased to one or two cells.
source: In α-adaptin mutants, the number of GFP-positive oocytes is decreased to one or two cells (Figure 5A,B), which is similar to the defect in μ2 mutants (Gu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on yolk endocytosis assay data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: The defect in YP170::GFP endocytosis in α-adaptin mutants is similar to the defect in μ2 mutants.
source: In α-adaptin mutants, the number of GFP-positive oocytes is decreased to one or two cells (Figure 5A,B), which is similar to the defect in μ2 mutants (Gu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a direct statement comparing the phenotypes, supported by citation and Figure 5A,B.

claim: Strong defects in YP170::GFP endocytosis are observed in mutants lacking the alternative clathrin adaptor Disabled.
source: By contrast, strong defects in YP170::GFP endocytosis are observed in mutants lacking the alternative clathrin adaptor Disabled (Holmes et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The AP2 complex appears to assist Disabled for yolk endocytosis.
source: Thus, the AP2 complex appears to assist Disabled for yolk endocytosis, and α- and μ2-adaptin do not contribute differentially to this process.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of phenotypes.

claim: α- and μ2-adaptin do not contribute differentially to yolk endocytosis.
source: Thus, the AP2 complex appears to assist Disabled for yolk endocytosis, and α- and μ2-adaptin do not contribute differentially to this process.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similar phenotypes of α and μ2 mutants.

claim: In wild-type worms, CD4-dileucine is localized to intracellular compartments.
source: In wild-type worms CD4-dileucine is localized to intracellular compartments; however, in apa-2 mutants CD4-dileucine accumulates abnormally on basolateral membranes (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on localization data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: In apa-2 mutants, CD4-dileucine accumulates abnormally on basolateral membranes.
source: In wild-type worms CD4-dileucine is localized to intracellular compartments; however, in apa-2 mutants CD4-dileucine accumulates abnormally on basolateral membranes (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on localization data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: In apm-2 mutants, the CD4-dileucine accumulation on the plasma membrane is milder (69% compared to α mutants).
source: By contrast in apm-2 mutants, the CD4-dileucine accumulation on the plasma membrane is milder (69% compared to α mutants; Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on quantification data shown in Figure 5D,E.

claim: Recovery of di-leucine cargo depends on α-adaptin more than μ2-adaptin.
source: These data suggest that recovery of di-leucine cargo depends on α-adaptin more than μ2-adaptin.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential accumulation of CD4-dileucine in α vs μ2 mutants.

claim: MIG-14/wntless is a μ2-dependent cargo.
source: MIG-14/wntless is a μ2-dependent cargo (Pan et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: In the absence of the μ2 subunit, MIG-14::GFP is strongly mislocalized to the basal and lateral surfaces of intestine cells.
source: In the absence of the μ2 subunit, MIG-14::GFP is strongly mislocalized to the basal and lateral surfaces of intestine cells (Figure 5F,G).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on localization data shown in Figure 5F,G.

claim: In the absence of α-adaptin, MIG-14::GFP is only weakly mislocalized on the basolateral surface (27% compared to μ2 mutants).
source: In the absence of α-adaptin, MIG-14::GFP is only weakly mislocalized on the basolateral surface (27% compared to μ2 mutants; Figure 5F,G).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on quantification data shown in Figure 5F,G.

claim: MIG-14 contains a tyrosine in its carboxy terminus.
source: MIG-14 contains a tyrosine in its carboxy terminus (μ2 consensus target is Yxxϕ), but it is not known if this sequence is required for μ2 binding.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the sequence of MIG-14.

claim: It is not known if the tyrosine sequence in MIG-14 is required for μ2 binding.
source: MIG-14 contains a tyrosine in its carboxy terminus (μ2 consensus target is Yxxϕ), but it is not known if this sequence is required for μ2 binding.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the lack of knowledge regarding the binding requirement.

claim: The endocytosis of clathrin-independent cargo hTAC is unaffected in both adaptin mutants.
source: As a control, the endocytosis of clathrin-independent cargo hTAC is unaffected in both adaptin mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on control experiment data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1, 2.

claim: Partially functional AP2 complexes might be present in mutations that eliminate single subunits.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that partially functional AP2 complexes might be present in mutations that eliminate single subunits.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cargo-specific defects observed.

claim: The open form of AP2 can be considered as two hemicomplexes: the α and the σ2 subunits are in close contact, and the μ2 and β subunits are in close contact.
source: The open form of AP2 can be considered as two hemicomplexes: the α and the σ2 subunits are in close contact, and the μ2 and β subunits are in close contact in both open and closed forms of the complex (Collins et al., 2002; Jackson et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior structural studies.

claim: The two hemicomplexes are only loosely associated in the open form of the AP2 complex.
source: However, these two hemicomplexes are only loosely associated in the open form of the AP2 complex (Jackson et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior structural studies.

claim: In the absence of α-adaptin, a μ2-β hemicomplex remains.
source: Here we demonstrate that in the absence of α-adaptin that a μ2-β hemicomplex remains, and that in the absence of μ2-adaptin that a α-σ2 complex remains in vivo.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on experimental observations of subunit stability and localization.

claim: In the absence of μ2-adaptin, a α-σ2 complex remains in vivo.
source: Here we demonstrate that in the absence of α-adaptin that a μ2-β hemicomplex remains, and that in the absence of μ2-adaptin that a α-σ2 complex remains in vivo.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on experimental observations of subunit stability and localization.

claim: The β- and μ2-adaptins are stable in the absence of α-adaptin.
source: The β- and μ2-adaptins, which are not closely associated with α-adaptin, are stable in the absence of α−adaptin.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on experimental observations of subunit stability.

claim: Tagged β-adaptin and μ2-adaptin are localized to synaptic regions of the nerve ring in apa-2 mutants.
source: Tagged β-adaptin and μ2-adaptin are localized to synaptic regions of the nerve ring (the major neuropil of the worm, Figure 6B,C) and at the plasma membrane in oocytes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on localization data shown in Figure 6B,C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The level of μ2-adaptin is reduced to 40% in apa-2 mutants as assayed by western blot.
source: The level of μ2-adaptin is reduced to 40% in apa-2 mutants as assayed by western blot (Figure 6—figure supplement 1) or 20% as measured by fluorescence (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The level of μ2-adaptin is reduced to 20% in apa-2 mutants as measured by fluorescence.
source: The level of μ2-adaptin is reduced to 40% in apa-2 mutants as assayed by western blot (Figure 6—figure supplement 1) or 20% as measured by fluorescence (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on fluorescence quantification shown in Figure 6.

claim: The small σ2 subunit is unstable in apa-2 mutants.
source: On the other hand, the small σ2 subunit, which is normally tightly bound to α-adaptin, is unstable in apa-2 mutants.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on experimental observations of subunit stability.

claim: Tagged σ2 is no longer detectable in the nerve ring in apa-2 mutants.
source: Tagged σ2 is no longer detectable in the nerve ring (Figure 6) or in maturing oocytes (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), and the protein is reduced to about 10% of the wild-type level as assayed by fluorescence (Figure 6, Table 1) or western blot (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on localization data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Tagged σ2 is no longer detectable in maturing oocytes in apa-2 mutants.
source: Tagged σ2 is no longer detectable in the nerve ring (Figure 6) or in maturing oocytes (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), and the protein is reduced to about 10% of the wild-type level as assayed by fluorescence (Figure 6, Table 1) or western blot (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on localization data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The σ2 protein is reduced to about 10% of the wild-type level in apa-2 mutants as assayed by fluorescence.
source: Tagged σ2 is no longer detectable in the nerve ring (Figure 6) or in maturing oocytes (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), and the protein is reduced to about 10% of the wild-type level as assayed by fluorescence (Figure 6, Table 1) or western blot (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on fluorescence quantification shown in Figure 6 and Table 1.

claim: Tagged α-adaptin is still localized to the synapse in apm-2 mutants.
source: Conversely, α-adaptin and σ2-adaptin are localized in the absence of μ2-adaptin. In apm-2 mutants, tagged α-adaptin is still localized to the synapse (Figure 6D) and the plasma membrane of coelomocytes.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on localization data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: α-adaptin levels are only reduced to 60% in apm-2 mutants as assayed by western blot.
source: α-adaptin levels are only reduced to 60% as assayed by western blot (Gu et al., 2008) or 40% as assayed by fluorescence.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: α-adaptin levels are reduced to 40% in apm-2 mutants as assayed by fluorescence.
source: α-adaptin levels are only reduced to 60% as assayed by western blot (Gu et al., 2008) or 40% as assayed by fluorescence.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on fluorescence quantification.

claim: Tagged σ2-adaptin is still localized to the nerve ring in apm-2 mutants.
source: Tagged σ2-adaptin is still localized to the nerve ring (Figure 6A) and is reduced to 40% as assayed by fluorescence (Figure 6, Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on localization data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Tagged σ2-adaptin is reduced to 40% in apm-2 mutants as assayed by fluorescence.
source: Tagged σ2-adaptin is still localized to the nerve ring (Figure 6A) and is reduced to 40% as assayed by fluorescence (Figure 6, Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on fluorescence quantification shown in Figure 6 and Table 1.

claim: The large β subunit is unstable in apm-2 mutants.
source: On the other hand, the large β subunit, which is normally tightly bound to μ2-adaptin, is unstable in apm-2 mutants.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on experimental observations of subunit stability.

claim: The β subunit is shared by AP1 and AP2 in C. elegans.
source: The β subunit is shared by AP1 and AP2 in C. elegans, and tagged β subunit fluorescence is visible in cell bodies in apm-2 mutants.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about C. elegans AP complexes.

claim: Tagged β is no longer detectable in the synapse-rich region of the nerve ring in the absence of μ2-adaptin.
source: However, tagged β is no longer detectable in the synapse-rich region of the nerve ring in the absence of μ2-adaptin (Figure 6B, Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on localization data shown in Figure 6B and Table 1.

claim: AP2 hemicomplexes are partially stable and can function in vivo in the absence of a complete AP2 complex.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that AP2 hemicomplexes are partially stable and can function in vivo in the absence of a complete AP2 complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the stability and localization data for individual subunits.

claim: AP2 components are required in the epidermis to play non-autonomous roles in synaptic development.
source: First, AP2 components are required in the epidermis to play non-autonomous roles in synaptic development (Gu et al., 2008; Pan et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: When α- and μ2-adaptins are simultaneously introduced back into the epidermis, 100% of the double mutants grow to adults.
source: However, when α- and μ2-adaptins are simultaneously introduced back into the epidermis, 100% of the double mutants grow to adults.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on rescue experiment observations.

claim: The skin-rescued apa-2 apm-2 double mutant worms have no detectable APA-2::GFP in the nervous system.
source: The skin-rescued worms have no detectable APA-2::GFP in the nervous system (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and the skin promoter Pdpy-7 is only expressed in larval stages during development (Johnstone and Barry, 1996).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on expression pattern data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The skin promoter Pdpy-7 is only expressed in larval stages during development.
source: The skin-rescued worms have no detectable APA-2::GFP in the nervous system (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and the skin promoter Pdpy-7 is only expressed in larval stages during development (Johnstone and Barry, 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: α-adaptin colocalizes with a synaptic vesicle protein, synaptobrevin, in both the dorsal and ventral nerve cords.
source: α-adaptin colocalizes with a synaptic vesicle protein, synaptobrevin, in both the dorsal and ventral nerve cords (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement based on colocalization data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: α-adaptin associates with synaptic varicosities.
